title: The Day of Judgment
subtitle: Why answering to God brings both warning and hope
summary: Islam teaches that death does not erase a life or settle every injustice. God raises the dead and judges with full knowledge, without inherited blame or special human privilege. The hope of final justice gives a reason to consider judgment. Belief that it will happen also needs evidence for the Creator and His revelation.

seo.metaTitle: The Day of Judgment: Quran and Bible Compared
seo.metaDescription: Islam's case for resurrection and final accountability: what the Quran says, why justice matters, and why moral hope alone is not proof.

sections.title: No Life Is Beyond God's Account
sections.body:
Islam teaches that every person will be raised and answer before God. Cruelty that escaped a court does not become harmless because its doer died. Quiet goodness does not become worthless because no one noticed.

This is both demanding and hopeful. The Judge knows the whole truth; reputation and power cannot decide the verdict. Judgment gives a reason to repair wrongs now rather than hide them.

sections.title: Why the Present World Is Not a Complete Court
sections.body:
Some wrongs can be exposed and repaired in a lifetime. Others cannot. Victims die without seeing justice, and people who acted bravely can be misjudged. If public success is the final verdict, those wrongs remain unresolved.

Islam does not take suffering as proof that its victims deserve it. It denies that visible events tell the whole moral story. Final judgment rests on God's knowledge, not the verdict that wealth, influence, or rumor has already produced.

sections.title: Does the Desire for Justice Prove a Judgment?
sections.body:
No. Wanting a just end does not make one exist. The hope of judgment explains why the question matters, but cannot prove a future event on its own.

Islam needs further grounds: a Creator able to restore life, and trustworthy revelation saying He will do so. [Why the Quran?](/articles/why-the-quran) addresses that second claim. The Quranic passages here explain the promised judgment. They are not, by themselves, proof to someone who has not yet accepted the Quran.

sections.title: Is Resurrection Impossible?
sections.body:
In the ordinary course of nature, the dead do not return to life. Islam does not dispute this. It presents resurrection as God's act, not an undiscovered medical treatment.

If the source of life exists and fully knows each person, human limits do not rule out His restoring that person. This answers a question about what is possible. It does not yet show that resurrection will happen; that still needs grounds for trusting revelation.

sections.title: What the Quran's Details Mean
sections.body:
Quran 99:6–8 says people will be shown their deeds, including the smallest good and evil. Quran 21:47 describes just scales and denies that a soul will be wronged. These passages insist on fairness, not a crude formula for buying Paradise.

Quran 84:7–8 describes an easy account, while 84:10 warns of a different way of receiving the record. Quran 17:15 keeps responsibility personal and links punishment with a messenger's warning. This is not a picture of everyone condemned alike. The setting in which a person responded also matters.

sections.title: Christian Teaching Also Takes Conduct Seriously
sections.body:
Revelation 20:12 describes opened books and judgment according to deeds. 2 Corinthians 5:10 and Romans 14:12 also make each person's account clear. A claim that Christians expect no reckoning for conduct would fail on these texts themselves.

Matthew 25:31–32 places the Son of Man in the judgment scene. [Orthodox teaching on judgment](https://www.oca.org/orthodoxy/the-orthodox-faith/doctrine-scripture/the-symbol-of-faith/judgment) presents Christ as judge, not as God's rival. The dispute with Islam concerns Jesus's identity and authority, not whether truth and deeds matter.

sections.title: Why Perfect Knowledge Matters
sections.body:
Human judgments can lack evidence, mistake motives, or favor the powerful. Islam promises a reckoning free of these faults. Rank and a polished public image cannot mislead the Creator about the person before Him.

This is why the Quran's scales and records matter. Nothing that bears on right and wrong is lost. That does not mean an observer can calculate someone else's final fate. Even a claimed religious identity stands before the Judge; it cannot become a cover for injustice.

sections.title: Can Someone Speak on Another's Behalf?
sections.body:
Intercession means asking God on someone else's behalf. It does not give anyone power to overrule Him. Quran 2:255 makes it depend on His permission. Answering directly to God does not rule out every form of intercession; it rules out a creature's separate power over His judgment.

Nor does hope in mercy make judgment needless. Forgiveness is not the claim that no harm occurred. [Forgiveness in Islam and Christianity](/articles/forgiveness-in-islam-and-christianity) examines mercy alongside the rights of those harmed.

sections.title: A Reason to Act, Not to Postpone Justice
sections.body:
Belief in final justice should make present duties more urgent. An unpaid debt still needs repayment; a false charge still needs correction; and a person in danger still needs help. Leaving everything to the Hereafter while refusing possible repair would betray the very duty to answer for one's acts.

Quran 99:7–8 also gives weight to small actions. A private act of honesty or care need not change public history to matter before God.

sections.title: Preparing With Hope and Humility
sections.body:
[Sin and Repentance](/articles/sin-and-repentance) gives a practical next step: name a wrong, stop it, and restore rights where possible. Preparing for judgment begins in this life, not in guesses about everyone else's fate.

Islam invites life before the One who knows all and whose judgment cannot be rigged. This allows hope without claiming a personal exemption, and care about wrongdoing without pretending to know God's final verdict on someone else.

sections.title: Frequently Asked Questions
sections.body:
Q: Does the need for justice prove life after death?
A: No. It explains why judgment matters. Belief that it will happen also needs grounds for believing in the Creator and trusting His revelation.

Q: Does the Quran's scale mean that deeds buy Paradise?
A: No. Quran 21:47 stresses that no soul is wronged. A fair judgment of deeds is not a price that forces God to grant eternal life.

Q: Does Islam deny all intercession?
A: No. Quran 2:255 allows it by God's permission. No creature can change or defeat His judgment through a separate power.

Q: Do Christians also teach accountability for deeds?
A: Yes. Revelation 20:12, 2 Corinthians 5:10, and Romans 14:12 describe an account of conduct, while Matthew 25 places Christ in the judgment scene.

sections.title: Sources and Further Reading
sections.body:
The Quran cards provide the selected passages on records, scales, responsibility, and permitted intercession. The Bible cards provide the Christian judgment texts discussed above.

The linked Orthodox explanation identifies Christ's role in its own theological terms. The studies below offer wider context; they do not replace the separate task of assessing a revelation claim.

quranVerses.arabic: يَوْمَئِذٍۢ يَصْدُرُ ٱلنَّاسُ أَشْتَاتًۭا لِّيُرَوْا۟ أَعْمَٰلَهُمْ
quranVerses.translation: That Day, the people will depart separated [into categories] to be shown [the result of] their deeds.
quranVerses.sourceAttribution: api.alquran.cloud — Tanzil Uthmani text; Saheeh International translation

quranVerses.arabic: فَمَن يَعْمَلْ مِثْقَالَ ذَرَّةٍ خَيْرًۭا يَرَهُۥ
quranVerses.translation: So whoever does an atom's weight of good will see it,
quranVerses.sourceAttribution: api.alquran.cloud — Tanzil Uthmani text; Saheeh International translation

quranVerses.arabic: وَمَن يَعْمَلْ مِثْقَالَ ذَرَّةٍۢ شَرًّۭا يَرَهُۥ
quranVerses.translation: And whoever does an atom's weight of evil will see it.
quranVerses.sourceAttribution: api.alquran.cloud — Tanzil Uthmani text; Saheeh International translation

quranVerses.arabic: وَنَضَعُ ٱلْمَوَٰزِينَ ٱلْقِسْطَ لِيَوْمِ ٱلْقِيَٰمَةِ فَلَا تُظْلَمُ نَفْسٌۭ شَيْـًۭٔا ۖ وَإِن كَانَ مِثْقَالَ حَبَّةٍۢ مِّنْ خَرْدَلٍ أَتَيْنَا بِهَا ۗ وَكَفَىٰ بِنَا حَٰسِبِينَ
quranVerses.translation: And We place the scales of justice for the Day of Resurrection, so no soul will be treated unjustly at all. And if there is [even] the weight of a mustard seed, We will bring it forth. And sufficient are We as accountant.
quranVerses.sourceAttribution: api.alquran.cloud — Tanzil Uthmani text; Saheeh International translation

quranVerses.translation: Then as for he who is given his record in his right hand,
quranVerses.sourceAttribution: api.alquran.cloud — Tanzil Uthmani text; Saheeh International translation

quranVerses.translation: He will be judged with an easy account
quranVerses.sourceAttribution: api.alquran.cloud — Tanzil Uthmani text; Saheeh International translation

quranVerses.arabic: مَّنِ ٱهْتَدَىٰ فَإِنَّمَا يَهْتَدِى لِنَفْسِهِۦ ۖ وَمَن ضَلَّ فَإِنَّمَا يَضِلُّ عَلَيْهَا ۚ وَلَا تَزِرُ وَازِرَةٌۭ وِزْرَ أُخْرَىٰ ۗ وَمَا كُنَّا مُعَذِّبِينَ حَتَّىٰ نَبْعَثَ رَسُولًۭا
quranVerses.translation: Whoever is guided is only guided for [the benefit of] his soul. And whoever errs only errs against it. And no bearer of burdens will bear the burden of another. And never would We punish until We sent a messenger.
quranVerses.sourceAttribution: api.alquran.cloud — Tanzil Uthmani text; Saheeh International translation

quranVerses.arabic: ٱللَّهُ لَآ إِلَٰهَ إِلَّا هُوَ ٱلْحَىُّ ٱلْقَيُّومُ ۚ لَا تَأْخُذُهُۥ سِنَةٌۭ وَلَا نَوْمٌۭ ۚ لَّهُۥ مَا فِى ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَمَا فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ ۗ مَن ذَا ٱلَّذِى يَشْفَعُ عِندَهُۥٓ إِلَّا بِإِذْنِهِۦ ۚ يَعْلَمُ مَا بَيْنَ أَيْدِيهِمْ وَمَا خَلْفَهُمْ ۖ وَلَا يُحِيطُونَ بِشَىْءٍۢ مِّنْ عِلْمِهِۦٓ إِلَّا بِمَا شَآءَ ۚ وَسِعَ كُرْسِيُّهُ ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلْأَرْضَ ۖ وَلَا يَـُٔودُهُۥ حِفْظُهُمَا ۚ وَهُوَ ٱلْعَلِىُّ ٱلْعَظِيمُ
quranVerses.translation: Allah - there is no deity except Him, the Ever-Living, the Sustainer of [all] existence. Neither drowsiness overtakes Him nor sleep. To Him belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth. Who is it that can intercede with Him except by His permission? He knows what is [presently] before them and what will be after them, and they encompass not a thing of His knowledge except for what He wills. His Kursi extends over the heavens and the earth, and their preservation tires Him not. And He is the Most High, the Most Great.
quranVerses.sourceAttribution: api.alquran.cloud — Tanzil Uthmani text; Saheeh International translation

quranVerses.arabic: وَأَمَّا مَنْ أُوتِىَ كِتَٰبَهُۥ وَرَآءَ ظَهْرِهِۦ
quranVerses.translation: But as for he who is given his record behind his back,
quranVerses.sourceAttribution: api.alquran.cloud — Tanzil Uthmani text; Saheeh International translation

bibleVerses.text:
“But when the Son of Man comes in his glory, and all the holy angels with him, then he will sit on the throne of his glory.

Before him all the nations will be gathered, and he will separate them one from another, as a shepherd separates the sheep from the goats.

I saw the dead, the great and the small, standing before the throne, and they opened books. Another book was opened, which is the book of life. The dead were judged out of the things which were written in the books, according to their works.
For we must all be revealed before the judgment seat of Christ; that each one may receive the things in the body, according to what he has done, whether good or bad.
So then each one of us will give account of himself to God.
Before him all the nations will be gathered, and he will separate them one from another, as a shepherd separates the sheep from the goats.
“But when the Son of Man comes in his glory, and all the holy angels with him, then he will sit on the throne of his glory.
